title: Why the Iran Deal Will Hold
gist: Foreign Policy video landing page (editor in chief Ravi Agrawal, 24 June 2026) arguing the Iran deal will hold; the captured text contains no transcript, only FP’s featured and related modules. Those modules show Agrawal’s own running theses — Iran as Trump’s greatest failure and the world paying for America’s war — alongside a live Strait of Hormuz reopening question and a fourth-year Sudan war.

insights.claim: Ravi Agrawal’s stated position is that Iran could turn out to be Trump’s greatest failure.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: Editorial-level conviction that the Iran policy ends badly argues for pricing sustained U.S. credibility discount rather than a clean post-deal normalisation.
insights.quote: Iran Could Be Trump’s Greatest Failure

insights.claim: Ravi Agrawal argues the world at large — not just the belligerents — is paying the price for America’s war.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: Frames the conflict as a global growth-and-inflation tax rather than a regional event, supporting a wider risk premium across energy-importing EM.
insights.quote: The World Is Paying the Price for America’s War

themes.theme: Hormuz reopening as the tradable variable

insights.claim: Adam Tooze has set out what reopening the Strait of Hormuz could look like, which implies the chokepoint was closed or materially disrupted during the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: The sequence and timing of a Hormuz reopening is the single biggest swing factor for crude curves and tanker day-rates.
insights.quote: What reopening the Strait of Hormuz could look like

insights.claim: The negotiated Iran agreement leaves the Strait of Hormuz hazy, so the chokepoint’s reopening is a matter of practice rather than settled treaty language.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: Ambiguity means shipping insurers, not diplomats, set the effective reopening date — track war-risk premia off Bandar Abbas.
insights.quote: The Iran Deal Is Hazy on Hormuz

insights.claim: The Sudan war has entered its fourth year.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: A grinding fourth-year Sudan conflict keeps Red Sea and Horn-of-Africa disruption structural and largely unpriced while attention sits on Iran.
insights.quote: The Sudan war enters its fourth year

insights.claim: Matthew Kroenig frames the strategic question as “What if China Succeeds?” — treating Chinese success, not Chinese collapse, as the scenario Western planners must price.
insights.speaker: Ravi Agrawal
insights.so_what: Planning for Chinese success inverts the consensus China-stagnation trade and argues for hedging long-duration exposure to Chinese technological and industrial capability.
